learn.canDo: Write a system prompt as separate, explicit rules with examples where needed, and see why compliance multiplies across rules.
learn.why: Most production prompt bugs are rules the prompt never stated or stated badly. A prompt is a spec you can test.

learn.canDo: Lay out a long prompt with documents first, tags, a few examples, and the question last, and test each choice.
learn.why: Layout is the cheapest lever on a long-context prompt, and a few points of accuracy cost almost nothing in tokens.
learn.keyIdea: Stable and long first, the question last.

learn.canDo: Set a thinking budget at the knee of the accuracy curve, and decide which tasks deserve reasoning tokens.
learn.why: Reasoning modes can turn a failing task into a working one, and they can burn money on tasks that never needed them.
learn.keyIdea: Spend thinking where the curve is steep.

learn.canDo: Get reliably parseable output with schemas and constrained decoding, and know what no schema guarantees.
learn.why: Parse errors at volume are a daily incident. A contract enforced by the decoder beats a polite request.
learn.keyIdea: Structure is enforced; truth is not.

learn.canDo: Lay out a prompt so a stable prefix is cached, and judge whether the hit rate justifies the write premium.
learn.why: Repeated context is the largest, easiest saving in most LLM bills, and one timestamp at the front can erase it.
learn.keyIdea: Stable prefix first; a change early breaks the rest.

learn.canDo: Version prompts, gate releases on a regression set, and size the set so noise does not hide real changes.
learn.why: A small wording tweak can quietly break a feature. A gate that ignores noise either misses regressions or blocks good changes.
learn.keyIdea: A small test set gives a number, not an answer.

chapter.story: Prompts become production code, and Pigeon learns that wording tweaks can break things quietly.
outcomes: Write system prompts as explicit, testable rules
Structure long prompts and choose examples
Spend reasoning tokens where they pay
Enforce output schemas, cache prefixes, and gate prompt releases
chapter.why: Once a prompt is in production it needs the discipline of any other code: a spec, a layout, a contract for its output, a cost model, and a release gate. This chapter gives each one a number.
chapter.payoff: You can describe how you would build and ship a prompt like an engineer, with the numbers to back each choice, which is the core of an AI-engineering interview.
